display.purpose: Monumental board numerals only. Tabular figures, read at arm's length in a dark room.

headline.purpose: Destination and area titles on yellow sign panels.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-copy on signage. The only role permitted uppercase.

motion.name: flap
motion.purpose: Split-flap character reveal on the gantry destination readout, staggered per character. The only expressive motion in the system.

components.name: Destination Row
components.description: One row of the junction board. The landing page is a stack of these; the emergency destination uses the alarm variant and always sits last.
components.html: 01SistemulPe unde intră sunetul și pe unde iese07Ceva nu mergeSimptom → ce verifici, în ordine

components.name: Area Band
components.description: Opens every section. A mid-page arrival always lands on a sign that names where it is. Quieter than the board on purpose: the numeral carries the colour and a single lit rule carries the edge, so seven sections do not become seven yellow walls. Red variant marks the emergency section.

components.name: Notice Panel
components.description: Framed signage panel with a pictogram inset square. Three intents only: neutral, stop (solid red prohibition), go (green pictogram). Never more than one per instruction row.
components.html:
Ordinea contează. Pornește consola prima și oprește-o ultima.

Nu urca niciodată faderul ca să acoperi un microfon de departe. Vei avea Larsen.

components.name: Keycap
components.description: A physical console button referenced in copy. Engraved chip in the body face — this is what keeps yellow reserved for wayfinding instead of being spent on inline emphasis.
components.html: Ține apăsat Sends on Faders mai mult de o secundă ca să rămână activ.

components.name: Gantry
components.description: The sign that always hangs above. Bottom-fixed on phones (thumb zone), top-fixed overhead at 900px+. Carries the current destination as a split-flap readout, the index button, and the emergency shortcut.
components.html: Ceva nu merge

narrative.overview:
This is not a documentation site. The reader is a volunteer standing at a mixing desk in a dim hall, on a phone, minutes before a service starts. They are not reading — they are navigating a building under time pressure. So the surface behaves like international terminal signage: a junction board of numbered destinations, a gantry sign that always says where you are, monumental numerals readable at arm's length, pictograms instead of decoration, and the channel signal path drawn as a transit line.

The palette is a Schiphol-lineage sign system rendered at night: matte black ground, internally-lit yellow panels with pure black type, white pictograms cut into black inset squares, red for prohibition and green for safe. One humanist family, Fira Sans, carries every voice through weight alone.

The world is deliberately the inverse of the site it replaced — gradient blobs, gradient headlines, pill tabs, badge rows, rounded cards and a blue/purple accent — the generic AI-default look the client rejected by name.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow is wayfinding and nothing else; spending it on emphasis breaks the system
Zero border-radius, zero shadows, zero gradients — hairline rules and value steps only
Night is the default because the room is dark; day mode is a token swap, not a second design
Monumental tabular numerals as the primary navigational landmark
Every diagram is hand-authored inline SVG that recolors with the mode
Content is static HTML so find-in-page works and the page survives JS being off

rules.name: The Yellow Budget
rules.body: #FFCC00 marks where to go and where you are. It never becomes body copy, an emphasis border, a hover tint, or a decorative fill. Console button names get an engraved keycap precisely so they never need yellow.

rules.name: Three Signals, No More
rules.body: Yellow wayfinding, red prohibition, green safe. Any fourth semantic color dilutes all three. Every colored state also carries a pictogram, a label, or a position so color is never the only carrier.

rules.name: Panels, Not Cards
rules.body: Hard rectangles, 1px hairline frames, black pictogram inset squares. Depth comes from ground/panel/panel-raised value separation. No shadow appears anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Thumb Zone
rules.body: The gantry sits at the bottom of the screen on phones because the reader is holding the device one-handed at a desk, and moves overhead at 900px where terminal signage belongs. Any change is checked at 390px in night mode first.

rules.name: One Voice, Four Weights
rules.body: Fira Sans only. No second family, no monospace, no italics. Hierarchy is weight and scale, never color. Uppercase is reserved for the signage label role.

dos: Do reserve yellow for wayfinding, red for danger, green for safe
Do lead every instruction with a numbered step — the reader is executing, not studying
Do draw new diagrams as inline SVG using the existing token classes so they follow the mode
Do keep new content as static HTML so find-in-page works
Do verify at 390px in night mode first; that is the real device
donts: Don't add a hero, a headline block, badge pills, or tag chips — the board is the entry point
Don't introduce a second font family, a monospace, or italics
Don't add rounded corners, shadows, gradients, or blur
Don't use color as the only carrier of meaning
Don't publish a fixed channel map — assignment changes per service
Don't state as manual fact anything absent from the official X32 manual
